course_outline_concepts: Best-of-N (Stiennon 2020) and why it's the cheap alternative to full RL — and its ceiling
On-policy vs off-policy for LM-RL (Tang 2024 analysis)
Replay buffers in RLHF: when useful, when they bias policy
Async actor-learner: OpenRLHF and verl's decoupling of rollout GPUs from trainer GPUs
Mini-batch sharing across prompts: per-prompt vs pooled advantages

sources.what_to_extract: Stiennon 2020 TL;DR RLHF baseline; BoN KL closed form log N − (N−1)/N; BoN-64 within ~2 pts of PPO at matched KL; first documented RM overoptimization curve (Figure 4).

Tang 2024 gap decomposition: ~80% distribution shift, ~20% variance; iterative DPO ≈ PPO on TL;DR / HH / GSM8K; Gemma-2B/7B; iterative recipe (per step: sample 2 responses from π_t, RM label, DPO β=0.1, frozen π_0 as ref).

Why trajectory replay fails in LLM RL (ratio explosion, stale advantages, KL-to-ref mismatch); TRL GRPOWithReplayBufferTrainer: prompt-level replay keyed by group-reward variance; p_i ∝ var_i + ε; DeepSeek-R1 §3.2 negative result on trajectory replay.

OpenRLHF async PPO architecture (rollout_queue, rollout_slots, vllm_lock, partial rollout); verl HybridFlow dataflow + priority + pause state; IMPALA V-trace ancestry; throughput 1.6–2.0× vs sync; staleness bound k = queue_depth + partial_rollout_depth; vllm_kl monitoring.
B × n packing; 1/(n−1) variance; n=8 sweet spot; framework defaults (verl rollout.n=8, TRL num_generations=8, OpenRLHF n_samples_per_prompt=4); prefix KV sharing across same-prompt rollouts in vLLM.

verl dual rollout backend (HFRollout reference / vllm_async_server.py production); engine-pause around line 628 on weight broadcast; priority field for partial rollout; SPMD sync retired via PR #4411; tokens-in / tokens-out async generate.

PolicyLoss returning (loss, clip_ratio, ppo_kl, vllm_kl); tis / icepop / seq-mask-tis IS correction; AdaptiveKLController; token-level KL reward factorization; correctness tools for async (IS clip, seq-mask, hard-cap drop).

Synchronous InstructGPT-shaped PPO loop; one-process rollout→score→GAE→N-epoch update; `kl` as reward shaping via `non_score_reward`; TRL has no cross-step replay or async rollout (baseline to contrast against).
Coverability framing: a source policy / dataset is useful iff it covers the target-optimal policy's support; win-rate-based source selection; why distribution shift is not just a number but a shape.

RSFT as the other BoN-flavored alternative (Llama 2 recipe): sample N, filter by RM/verifier, SFT on survivors; sits one rung above BoN on the ceiling but still below on-policy RL; legitimate first-iteration move before PPO.
